content.text: The text recounts the execution of Louis XVI, Marie Antoinette, Madame Elisabeth, and the suffering and death of Louis XVII in the Temple Tower. Louis goes from the Temple to the scaffold; Marie Antoinette is moved from the Temple to the Conciergerie and later executed. Madame Royale is released from the Temple, travels to Vienna and Mittau, marries the Duc d’Angoulême, and later lives in exile. The narrative then shifts to Mugsborough workers: Bert pushes supplies up a long hill to the Cave; Owen visits Rushton’s office, designs the Cave’s drawing-room, and debates poverty and capitalism. Easton and Ruth let Slyme a bedroom. Workers gather at the Cricketers Arms, while Frankie attends the Shining Light Chapel. The text criticizes exploitation, religion, municipal corruption, wage reductions, unemployment, and the “Great Money Trick” by which capitalists control workers.
